findings.title: Client map-role permission checks bypass the manage-clients admin role
findings.body: In ClientPermissionsV2, canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles only call hasPermission(client, <scope>). They do not first check root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) or otherwise delegate to canManage(), unlike canManage(client), canConfigure(client), canManageClientScopes(), and the V1 semantics for these operations. As a result, an administrator holding the realm manage-clients role but no explicit fine-grained map-roles/map-roles-composite/map-roles-client-scope permission is denied these client role operations when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. The methods should preserve the admin-role bypass before evaluating fine-grained scopes.

findings.title: V2 authorization cleanup is skipped on role/client/group removal
findings.body: The listener now runs its cleanup only when the legacy ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature is enabled. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled by itself, AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, but this block does not execute, so client/role/group removal does not clean up the corresponding admin-permission resources or policies in V2. Additionally, ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled currently throws UnsupportedOperationException, so if both feature flags are enabled the guard passes and deletion events can hit that exception. The result is stale authorization resources/policies for deleted objects, potentially causing incorrect permission listings and evaluation state.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the all-clients resource name as a client ID
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates over every resource of type CLIENTS, including the special all-clients resource whose name is AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE ("Clients"). If hasGrantedPermission() is true for that resource, the code adds resource.getName() to a set that callers treat as actual client IDs. With a type-level "all clients" permission the returned set contains "Clients" instead of all real client IDs, so callers filtering clients can end up with no matching clients or a bogus client ID. The all-resource case must be expanded to actual client IDs or otherwise handled explicitly, and the resource-type resource name must not be returned as a client ID.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new Clients resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema now registers CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and creates client resources with name = client.getId() and no display name in getOrCreateResource. However getResourceName still only has a branch for USERS. For a policy with resource type Clients, including the all-clients resource, it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null for these resources or at best the raw client UUID, and it never returns an "All clients"-style display. This leaves the new client resource type without a proper human-readable resource name in permission representations. A CLIENTS branch symmetric to USERS is needed, resolving client IDs to clientId and mapping the type resource to a display such as "All clients".
